observation.visible_scene: A row of lantern-style street lamps mounted on a building wall at dusk, viewed from a fixed angle. The nearest lamp dominates the left-center, with progressively smaller lamps receding toward the right along the facade; a dark teal evening sky fills the right edge. The architecture, windows, and lamp positions remain unchanged throughout.
visible_changes: The lamps' warm glow pulses continuously: the halo/bloom around each lantern expands and softens, then contracts and sharpens, repeating across the segment.

During peak bloom (roughly frames 10-22 and again 40-41) the nearest lamp's internal panes and flame shape wash out into a bright diffuse orb; during the dimmer phases (frames 24-39) the lantern's glass panes and inner core become crisp and defined again.
The mid-distance and far lamps brighten and dim in roughly the same rhythm as the foreground lamp, so the whole row appears to breathe/flicker together.
No lamp or building shifts position; the change is in light intensity and bloom, not translation or deformation of the fixtures.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the pulsing glow (real flame flicker, electrical flicker, or a rendered glow animation) is not shown.
Whether the pulse is periodic or random cannot be determined from this short crop; the pattern is already in progress at the first frame and still ongoing at the last.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the framing looks static, but tiny sub-pixel drift cannot be ruled out.
Exact timing/synchronization of each lamp's pulse is approximate; the distant lamps are too small to track precisely.
